summary: Record the first executable controller skeleton as a cross-cutting behavioral implementation change requiring full five-stage review before further implementation proceeds.
reason: Revision 2 Adversarial revalidation found that StateSnapshot still trusted Python annotations for authoritative field types, allowing raw strings or other wrong-typed values to bypass enum-based invariants and reach persistence. Revision 3 adds deterministic runtime validation for every authoritative StateSnapshot field type and focused regression coverage, including the raw program_state='active' plus missing-stage-cursor bypass. Because this correction changes the authoritative state construction boundary, the review reopens at Adversarial and the full five-stage program remains required before implementation may continue beyond the skeleton.

reasons: This execution unit covers only the revision-3 Adversarial revalidation of the corrected controller-core skeleton; the other four semantic stages remain separate later execution units.

The corrected governed surface remains small and cohesive enough to retest failure, replay, authority-bypass, mutation, stale-state, representability, and recovery risks in one bounded Adversarial pass.

workload.notes: Revision-3 full-program Adversarial revalidation under SEPARATED execution; no semantic stage credit is created by this gate.

capability.benchmark_evidence: Built-in separated default; not a claim of measured reviewer capability.

decision.assurance_boundary: Semantic judgment determines whether one pass is suitable and which bounded subpasses require isolation. Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. The gate and completion validator enforce the recorded plan but do not prove the semantic assessment itself was correct.
